title: Adoption by any product
statement: A product adopts Lathe in its own repo and adds the kinds it needs without forking the schema.
measure: The product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package with its schema unchanged, counted from the installs the Owner knows of.
target: At least two such product repos, none with a forked schema, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner counts the product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package, from the installs they know of, and looks in each for a schema of its own; no test or record in this repo can see another repo.

title: Right first time
statement: An Agent that builds from the spec gets the change right the first time: what it builds matches the use cases, rules and tests it was given, so the change merges without being sent back.
measure: The share of an Agent's changes built from the spec that merge into main without rework (no send-back for a missed requirement or rule, and no fix-up commit on the same work before it merges), counted each month from the merges the Owner reviews.
target: At least 80% within three months of the first published release, and 90% within a year.
measured_outside: The Owner tallies each month, from the branches they review and merge, which of an Agent's changes merged as first handed in and which were sent back or needed a fix-up for something the spec said; no test in this repo sees the review.

title: Status from the spec
statement: The Owner learns what is built, proved or still missing from the spec itself, without asking an Agent.
measure: The status questions the Owner still has to ask an Agent each week (what is done, what is tested, what is left) because the spec and its coverage could not answer them.
target: At most one such question a week, within three months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner keeps a tally of the status questions they ask Agents each week that the spec could not answer; the coverage that `lathe check` prints is what should make them unnecessary.

title: Fewer regressions on main
statement: Mistakes a requirement or rule would have caught are caught before they merge, not found later on main.
measure: Defects found on main after a merge that a requirement, rule or test written in the spec would have caught, counted per month.
target: At most one a month, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner records each defect found on main after a merge and judges whether a requirement, rule or test in the spec would have caught it, counting them each month from the fixes they merge.

title: Quick idea to proof
statement: A new piece of behavior goes from written down to built and proved quickly, because the spec tells the Agent exactly what to build and test.
measure: The median time from a new use case being written to all of its tests passing, over the use cases written each month.
target: A median under two days, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner takes, from git, when each new use case was added and when its last test first passed on main, and works out the median each month; the dates live in the history, not in a test.

title: Newcomers find their way
statement: A new Agent or Reader, meeting a product for the first time, finds the code and tests behind a requirement quickly from the spec and the app.
measure: The time a new Agent or Reader takes to find the code and the tests behind a requirement they are given, timed in a short trial on a product they have not seen.
target: Under five minutes, median over the trials, within three months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner runs the trial with each new Agent or Reader: names a requirement, times how long it takes them to name its code file and its tests, and keeps the median.
